grammar.title: Present simple: câu khẳng định, phủ định, nghi vấn
grammar.html:
Khẳng định: I/you/we/they + V; he/she/it + V-s/es.
Phủ định: don't / doesn't + V (nguyên mẫu).
Nghi vấn: Do/Does + chủ ngữ + V?

Trạng từ tần suất (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never) đứng trước động từ thường và sau to be: She always visits… / She is always…

Bị động hiện tại đơn: am/is/are + V3: Rice is grown in the south.

exercises.passage:
Making friends in a new city

Moving to a new city can be exciting, but it can also feel lonely. When Linh moved from a small village to Ho Chi Minh City to study, she did not know anyone. For the first month, she spent most evenings alone in her room.

Then a classmate invited her to a weekend get-together. At first, Linh felt shy, but the other students were friendly and asked her many questions. She discovered that two of them also came from villages. They talked about missing their families and about the dishes they loved to cook.

After that evening, Linh joined the university English club. Now she meets her new friends twice a week. She says that a good friend is someone who is reliable and listens carefully. "I am still homesick sometimes," she admits, "but I do not feel alone any more."

grammar.title: There is / There are, so sánh và quantifiers
grammar.html:
There is + danh từ số ít/không đếm được; There are + danh từ số nhiều.
So sánh hơn: tính từ ngắn + -er than (quieter than); tính từ dài: more + adj + than (more crowded than).
So sánh nhất: the + adj-est / the most + adj.

Quantifiers: many/a few/several + danh từ đếm được số nhiều; much/a little + danh từ không đếm được; a lot of dùng cho cả hai.

items.html: Choose the correct answer.

opts: There were no factories or university.

items.q: What connects Dong Phu to the coast?

opts: to build a park and plant trees

items.html: Answer the questions. Use no more than THREE words.

items.q: What did most people grow in the past?
How many modern hotels are there?
Which place is still the most popular?

exercises.passage:
A town that changed

Ten years ago, Dong Phu was a quiet farming town. Most people grew rice, and there were only two small shops on the main street. Young people often left to find work in the big cities, because the town had no factories and no university.

Today, the town looks very different. A new road connects Dong Phu to the coast, and a large shopping centre opened last year. Visitors can stay in one of three modern hotels or walk through the old market, which is still the most popular place in town.

Not everyone is happy about the changes. Some older residents say that the streets are now too crowded and that traffic causes noise and pollution. The mayor has promised to build a park and to plant more trees along the river, so that Dong Phu stays a pleasant place to live.

grammar.title: Past simple và Present perfect (for / since)
grammar.html:
Past simple (V-ed / bất quy tắc) dùng cho hành động đã kết thúc tại thời điểm xác định: She graduated in 2020.

Present perfect (have/has + V3) dùng cho việc bắt đầu trong quá khứ và còn liên quan hiện tại, hoặc kinh nghiệm: I have worked here for three years.

for + khoảng thời gian (for five years); since + mốc thời gian (since 2018). yet trong câu phủ định/nghi vấn: I haven't finished yet.

exercises.passage:
Learning while working

In many countries, young people can combine study and work through apprenticeships. Minh, who is nineteen, spends three days a week at a car factory and two days at a technical college. He earns a small salary and does not have to pay for his course.

"At first I was nervous because everything was new," Minh says. "My supervisor showed me how to use the machines safely, and my colleagues were very patient." After six months, he could repair simple engine problems on his own.

Not every student likes this system. Some say it is tiring to study and work in the same week. Others worry that they will miss the social life of a university. However, studies show that most apprentices find a full-time job within three months of finishing their course, which is faster than many graduates.

grammar.title: Danh từ đếm được / không đếm được và các từ chỉ số lượng

Đếm được (egg – eggs, apple – apples) và không đếm được (water, rice, sugar, milk).

some dùng trong câu khẳng định và lời mời/đề nghị (Would you like some tea?); any dùng trong câu phủ định và nghi vấn.

exercises.passage:
A bowl of noodles for breakfast

In Vietnam, many people eat breakfast outside the home. Street sellers start work before sunrise, preparing broth, noodles and fresh herbs. A bowl of noodle soup costs about forty thousand dong, and customers often sit on small plastic stools on the pavement.

Doctors say that a traditional breakfast like this can be healthy because it contains protein from meat or tofu, carbohydrates from noodles and vitamins from vegetables. However, some stalls use a lot of salt, so it is better not to drink all of the soup.

Today more young people are choosing fast food or sweet drinks for breakfast because they are in a hurry. A recent survey in one city found that 40 per cent of students skip breakfast on school days. Teachers are worried because children who do not eat breakfast often find it difficult to concentrate in the morning.

grammar.html:
will + V: quyết định tức thời, dự đoán, lời hứa (I think I'll take the blue one.).
be going to + V: kế hoạch đã có hoặc dự đoán dựa trên bằng chứng (Look at those clouds. It is going to rain.).

exercises.passage:
Why do we buy things we do not need?

Every day, shoppers around the world buy things they do not really need. Psychologists say that advertisements and sales are partly responsible. When a shop offers a big discount, customers feel that they are saving money, even if they are actually spending more than they planned.

Social media makes the problem bigger. People see friends and famous bloggers wearing new clothes and using new gadgets, and they want the same things. One study found that young adults who spend more than three hours a day on social media buy clothes twice as often as those who spend less than one hour.

Experts suggest a few simple rules to control spending. Write a shopping list before you go out, wait 24 hours before buying expensive items, and read reviews from real customers. Some families also have a "no-spend" day each week to remind themselves that happiness does not depend on shopping.

exercises.passage:
The return of board games

In recent years, board games have become popular again, especially among young adults. Cafés where customers can play games with friends have opened in many cities. A typical café offers more than three hundred different games, and people usually pay a small fee for each hour.

Fans say that board games are a good way to relax without a screen. Players have to talk to each other, so the games are also social. Teachers like them too, because many games teach children to plan, count and solve problems.

However, some players complain that good games are expensive. One popular game costs about two million dong, which is a lot for a student. For this reason, many cafés allow members to borrow games or to try them for free before they decide to buy.

exercises.passage:
Life as an influencer

Twenty-two-year-old Hoa is one of the best-known young influencers in her city. She started posting videos about cooking at the age of seventeen, and her channel now has more than 800,000 followers. Companies send her free products and pay her to mention them in her videos.

Hoa admits that her job is not as easy as it looks. She spends about six hours making a video that lasts only ten minutes, and she must answer hundreds of messages every week. "People think I only film for fun," she says, "but I also do research, shopping and editing."

The hardest part, according to Hoa, is the lack of privacy. Strangers sometimes recognise her in restaurants and take photos without asking. She has learned to ignore negative comments, but she warns young people that fame on the internet can disappear as quickly as it arrives.

grammar.title: Động từ khuyết thiếu: must, have to, should, might, can't
grammar.html:
must / have to: bắt buộc (All visitors must wear a life jacket.). mustn't: cấm (You mustn't feed the animals.). don't have to: không cần thiết, không bắt buộc.

should / shouldn't: lời khuyên. might: có thể (không chắc). must be / can't be: suy đoán chắc chắn (He can't be at home. His car isn't here.).

exercises.passage:
Saving the sea turtles

Every year, thousands of sea turtles come to the beaches of Con Dao to lay their eggs. The females dig holes in the sand at night, lay about one hundred eggs, and return to the sea. Two months later, the baby turtles come out and race towards the water.

Sadly, sea turtles are endangered. Plastic rubbish in the ocean is a serious danger because turtles often mistake plastic bags for jellyfish and eat them. In addition, bright lights from hotels confuse the babies, so they walk in the wrong direction. Conservation workers now collect the eggs and keep them in safe areas until they hatch.

Volunteers also teach local children about the problem. Tourists are asked to use less plastic and to switch off lights near the beach at night. Thanks to these efforts, the number of nests has increased by 20 per cent in the last five years, but experts say that much more work is needed.
